item.title: Magic Tiles Strain Now Puts Phantom Tiles in the Starting Pool (1.5.6)
item.description:
MID GAME

The entire 1.5.6 line about Magic Tiles is one sentence: phantom tiles are now in the pool of tiles available at the start. If you were treating your opening board as a fixed set of possibilities, that sentence changes what you check in staging.

It is a pool change, not a new tile. The tile and its behaviour already existed. What 1.5.6 changed is that the Strain can now offer it among the tiles available when a run begins.

item.title: Quick Restart No Longer Wipes Gambit Medal Progress After 1.5.4b
item.description:
MID GAME

Losing progress is the one bug that changes how people play. If a restart looks like it wipes your medal, you stop restarting, and that is a much bigger cost than the medal itself.

1.5.4b lists it under fixes, not changes. Fixed an issue where Gambit Medal progress would reset after using Quick Restart. The progress was always supposed to stay.

item.title: First 3 Turns: The Universal Safe Opening Template (Works With Any Seed in Gambonanza)
item.description:
First 3 Turns: The Universal Safe Opening Template (Works With Any Seed in Gambonanza)

You start a run and your first 3 turns decide whether you see the Stage 2 boss.

That is not an exaggeration. After 50+ documented runs across every board size and dozens of seeds, my data shows a clear pattern: players who follow a universal safe opening in the first 3 turns survive to Stage 2 far more often than players who improvise. The opening is not about finding the perfect seed or memorizing a niche build. It is about three simple, repeatable decisions that work no matter what the game throws at you.

item.title: Gambonanza Difficulty Guide - What Changes as You Climb
item.description:
You do not choose a difficulty on your first run. The difficulty tiers unlock only after you finish a full clear. So the first run is about learning the board, and the climb starts after that.

Gambonanza gates its difficulty behind progress. Finish a run once, and the higher tiers open up in sequence. Each one stacks negative modifiers on top of the last.

How the Difficulty System Works

Stage State What changes
First runs Default tier Learn the board, Gambit triggers, and the boss preview
After first clear Tiers unlock Six tiers open in order, named after chess pieces starting with Rook and Knight
Higher tiers Stacked modifiers Each tier adds negative modifiers that constrain your run
Top tiers Hidden content An extra boss appears beyond the standard 8-boss roster

item.title: Unlocked King Difficulty and Die Every Run? 4 Hidden Mechanic Changes That Are Killing You
item.description:
' last_reviewed: “2026-09-26” review_status: “current”

You beat Queen difficulty. You unlock King. You play exactly the same way and die by Stage 2.

I have been there. The community has been there. And for weeks, the conversation was the same: “King is just harder, keep grinding.” But that is not the full story. King difficulty does not simply increase enemy stats. It changes the underlying rules of the game. The pricing model. The boss scaling formula. The board collapse timer. The AI targeting logic. All of it shifts in ways the game never explicitly tells you.
